sections.content:
12,405 people

were counted on the census as "textile process operatives" in England and Wales in March 2021.

Textile process operatives operate machines to prepare natural and synthetic fibres for processing, spin and twist fibre into yarn, thread, twine, rope and other similar material, and estimate the quantities of colouring matter required for printing and dyeing fabrics.

People who had this job were generally similar in age to the working population

The occupation of "textile process operatives" had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 50 to 54 years. Of the whole working population 11.7% were aged 50 to 54 years. For people working as "textile process operatives", 13% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "textile process operatives" was 16 to 19 years.

sections.content:
Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "textile process operatives" included:

  • assemblers (electrical and electronic products)
  • fishmongers and poultry dressers
  • furniture makers and other craft woodworkers

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

More men than women had this job

Among people working as "textile process operatives" there were more men than women (63.2% compared with 36.8%).

This means "textile process operatives" had a different proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "process, plant and machine operatives".

Men made up 63.2% and women made up 36.8% of "textile process operatives"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women. This occupation was one of the jobs for which the proportion of men and women was closest to this overall picture.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "textile process operatives" included:

  • business sales executives
  • assemblers and routine operatives (other)
  • quality control and planning engineers

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

We can look at who worked as "textile process operatives" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Men and women with this occupation had a similar age profile, as shown in the chart below.

The percentage of men and women who are "textile process operatives" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "textile process operatives", 8.8% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (77.2% compared with 22.8%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (88.9%) than self-employed (11.1%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the North West. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Kirklees, this is in the region of the Yorkshire & Humberside.
